newsitem.title: FRANCE: IRAQ BUYS 50,000 TONNES U.S. WHEAT - TRADERS.
newsitem.headline: IRAQ BUYS 50,000 TONNES U.S. WHEAT - TRADERS.

text.p: Iraq has bought 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat at $187 per tonne including freight for delivery to the port of Umm Qasr, European traders said on Wednesday.
Timing of the delivery was not immediately clear, amid conflicting reports over the contract terms, but one trader said the wheat was expected to reach Iraq in September.
Contents of the overnight grain deal reached markets shortly after Iraq announced it expected to resume crude exports under an oil-for-food deal with the United Nations by mid-August.

It is the first grain deal since oil exports were delayed while a new aid distribution plan was negotiated for Iraq. It is also the first publicly-reported Iraqi grain purchase of the 1997/98 crop year, although the delivery of some grain bought in the previous season is said to have been delayed.
Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the UN was set up to alleviate the impact on civilians of sanctions imposed on the country after its troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990.

Its second phase allows Baghdad to export $2.14 billion of oil over 180 days starting from June 8. Exports were delayed while the new aid plan was put in place, meaning Baghdad must sell around $1 billion of oil by September 5 or forego some of its allowance.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said in Baghdad on Wednesday Iraq planned to resume oil exports by mid-August.

Exports under the first six-month phase of the agreement, which started last December, averaged nearly 700,000 barrels per day. Using part of the revenues that went into U.N. escrow accounts from this phase of the deal, Baghdad bought an estimated 1.3 million tonnes of wheat from suppliers including Australia, France, Argentina and the United States.
